data.name: Jawwad
data.gender_notes: Jawwad is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Jawwad is an Arabic name for boys that means 'generous, liberal, bountiful'. It is derived from the J-W-D root which is used in many places in the Quran. The name Jawwad carries the meaning “Generous” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in English, Urdu, Hindi. Parents who choose Jawwad usually hope their child will grow to embody generous and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: To be generous is a way of life in Islam. It signifies the wealth and prosperity that Allah bestows upon us, and the responsibility we have to share it with others. A generous person is a reflection of Allah's mercy and compassion.
data.etymology: Jawwad belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Generous.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jawwad total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_english.name: Jawwad
in_english.meaning: Generous, liberal, one who gives abundantly
in_english.long_meaning: The name Jawwad originates from the Arabic root 'j-w-d' which means 'to give' or 'to bestow'. It signifies generosity, liberality, and abundance. In Islamic tradition, Al-Jawwad is one of the attributes of Allah mentioned in the Quran, specifically in Surah Al-Hajj (22:46) and Surah Sad (38:34). The name embodies the qualities of a generous and charitable person. Historically, it has been used across various Muslim cultures, symbolizing the ideal of being a benefactor and a do-gooder.

data.cultural_impact: The name Jawwad reflects a societal value placed on generosity and generosity in Arab culture. In traditional Arab societies, being known as a generous figure is considered a great honor. This is not only true in a material sense, but also in a more abstract sense of considering an individual's time, attention, and knowledge as valuable gifts to share with others. This name reflects a belief that hospitality and kindness are essential components of a prosperous and harmonious community.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Jawwad embodies the concept of inner richness and contentment, which is a central tenet of Islamic teachings. Prophet Muhammad (PBUH) is reported to have said, "The believer's shade on the Day of Resurrection will be his charity." This statement reinforces the idea that generosity is not only a significant act in the material world, but also a crucial component of an individual's spiritual growth. By living a generous life, a person not only enriches their community, but also deepens their connection to their Creator. Thus, Jawwad as a name reflects a spiritual calling to embody the qualities of generosity and selflessness in every aspect of life.
